content.text: This is a well-known OWASP Benchmark test case for command injection. Let me view the rest of the file to confirm the taint flow.

This confirms the classic OWASP Benchmark command injection pattern: `param` is read from a user-controlled HTTP header (`BenchmarkTest00017`), URL-decoded (no sanitization against command injection), and concatenated directly into `r.exec(cmd + param)`. There is no validation/sanitization breaking the taint flow.

input.justification:
The value `param` originates from a user-controlled HTTP header (request.getHeaders("BenchmarkTest00017")), is URL-decoded (which does not sanitize against command injection), and is then concatenated directly into a string passed to Runtime.exec(cmd + param). No validation, allow-listing, or encoding that would prevent command injection occurs between the source and the sink. This matches the well-known OWASP Benchmark command injection test case pattern, which is intentionally vulnerable.</justification>
